practice_description.medium: immersive audiovisual installation, sound art, data visualization, live performance, publication
practice_description.practice_summary: Japanese sound and visual artist who transforms vast datasets — DNA sequences, astronomical coordinates, mathematical structures — into immersive sensory experiences. His practice makes data legible not through comprehension but through sensory overwhelm, rendering the invisible multi-substance of data perceptible as light, sound, and spatial experience.
practice_description.methodology: Ikeda works with pure data as primary material, applying mathematical principles to generate every pixel and every sound event. He sources scientific datasets (genomics, astrophysics, particle physics, molecular biology) and processes them through custom software and mathematical transformations to produce synchronized audiovisual compositions. The work moves through dimensional scales — from 2D pattern sequences derived from hard drive errors and software code, through 3D rotating universe views, to 4D mathematical processing. His installations are precisely calibrated: black-and-white with striking color accents, minimal yet intense, operating at the threshold of human perception. He elaborately orchestrates sound, visuals, materials, physical phenomena and mathematical notions into unified experiences.

relevance_to_sense_room.relevance_summary: Ikeda demonstrates how raw data can become the primary material of immersive art — making graph data and relational structures directly experienceable as sensory phenomena. His practice provides a model for how A(DAI)'s intelligence graph could manifest as spatial experience rather than information display.
relevance_to_sense_room.art_as_substrate: Yes. Ikeda's data-driven visual and sonic fields function as total environmental substrates — visitors are literally immersed in projected data, lying on floors surrounded by sound. The artwork IS the environment.
relevance_to_sense_room.relational_composition: Partially. Ikeda's compositions are driven by mathematical relationships within datasets — correlations, transformations, dimensional mappings. However, the relational structure is between data points rather than between autonomous artwork elements.
relevance_to_sense_room.self_recomposing: Partially. While installations like datamatics are precisely composed rather than generative in real-time, some works respond to live data inputs. The data-verse series processes data through transformations that produce continuously evolving audiovisual sequences.

works.title: datamatics
works.description: Multi-format art project exploring perception of invisible data. Manifests as audiovisual concerts, installations, publications, and recordings. Uses pure data — hard drive errors, software code, astronomical coordinates — as source for synchronized black-and-white projections with sound.
works.relevance: Foundational demonstration of data-as-art-material. Shows how heterogeneous datasets can be transformed into unified sensory experience — a model for how graph data could become exhibition material.

works.title: the planck universe [macro] / [micro]
works.description: Installation exploring the extremes of physical scale — from quantum to cosmic — using data from particle physics and astrophysics. Mathematical processing opens up seemingly infinite vistas of data visualization.
works.relevance: Demonstrates art operating across scales of data complexity, from microscopic to macroscopic — relevant to how A(DAI)'s graph could be experienced at different levels of granularity.

works.title: data-verse
works.description: Commissioned by Audemars Piguet Contemporary. Seven-chapter immersive installation charting data from particle physics to astrophysics. Toured internationally, U.S. debut at High Museum of Art. Each chapter presents an encounter between human comprehension limits and audiovisual representations of limitlessness.
works.relevance: Large-scale model for how data can be exhibited as immersive spatial experience in major museum contexts — demonstrates institutional viability of data-as-art exhibitions.

protocol_art_resonance.protocol_art_summary: Ikeda does not treat systems or protocols as medium in the governance/infrastructure sense. His practice is about making existing data systems perceptible — aestheticizing data rather than designing new protocols. The mathematical transformations he applies are artistic tools rather than infrastructure contributions.
protocol_art_resonance.system_designed: Custom audiovisual rendering systems for data transformation. No infrastructure or protocol designed for external use — his systems are bespoke tools for his own artistic production.

commons_orientation.commons_summary: Ikeda operates within the commercial gallery and museum system. His works are proprietary — commissioned by institutions (Audemars Piguet, 180 Studios) and shown in major venues. While he uses scientific datasets that are often public domain, his artistic software and methods are not shared. No commons infrastructure contribution.

governance_model.governance_detail: Solo artist practice. Ikeda conceives, designs, and controls all aspects of his work. Technical implementation involves studio collaborators but artistic direction is singular. Commissions and exhibitions are managed through standard gallery/institutional relationships.

consent_and_authorship.consent_approach: Uses publicly available scientific datasets (genomics, astrophysics, particle physics). No consent issues with data sources as they are public domain scientific data. Audience members are passive immersive participants.
consent_and_authorship.authorship_model: Solo. All works attributed to Ryoji Ikeda. Technical collaborators are uncredited in the artistic output.

liveness_and_duration.temporal_detail: Installations run for exhibition duration as precisely composed sequences. Audiovisual concerts are live performances with defined duration. While the data-driven imagery evolves continuously within a piece, the works are composed rather than open-endedly generative — they have defined sequences and structures that cycle through mathematical transformations.

data_materiality.data_sources: Scientific datasets: DNA human genome sequences, astronomical coordinates of stars, molecular structures of proteins, particle physics data, hard drive error data, software code architecture, mathematical structures (Planck scale data).
data_materiality.data_provenance: Public domain scientific data. Datasets sourced from research institutions, astronomical databases, genomic databases, and mathematical/physical constants. Clean provenance — publicly available scientific knowledge.

embedding_space_relevance.embedding_summary: Ikeda does not work with ML embedding spaces. However, his practice of mapping high-dimensional scientific data into audiovisual space is conceptually analogous to dimensionality reduction and embedding visualization — making high-dimensional data perceptible through lower-dimensional sensory mappings.
embedding_space_relevance.multimodal: Yes — his work fundamentally spans audio and visual modalities in tightly synchronized compositions. Data is simultaneously rendered as sound and image within unified installations.

exhibition_modality.spatial_description: Large-scale immersive installations with floor-to-ceiling projections (sometimes projected onto both wall and floor from 8K sources). Visitors lie on floors surrounded by projected data and enveloping sound. Precise architectural control of light and acoustic environment. Also manifests as audiovisual concerts with massive projection screens. Exhibited at 180 Studios London, High Museum of Art Atlanta, MACBA Barcelona, Centre Pompidou Paris, and many others.

interoperability.composability: Low. Ikeda's installations are self-contained total environments. The works do not expose APIs or produce outputs designed for reuse. Each piece is a closed, precisely calibrated system.
interoperability.technical_openness: Closed system. Proprietary custom software, no open-source components, no documentation of tools.

technical_approach.stack: Custom software for data processing and audiovisual rendering, Max/MSP and Jitter (widely attributed by community though not officially confirmed), possibly Pure Data and Processing, precise signal generators, multi-projector systems (up to 8K), custom sound systems, mathematical/algorithmic composition tools

network_position.scene_affiliation: Central figure bridging electronic music, sound art, data art, and contemporary art installation. Connected to minimal electronic music scene (Alva Noto/Carsten Nicolai, Autechre), media art institutions (Ars Electronica, ZKM), major contemporary art institutions (Centre Pompidou, Tate), and the luxury brand art patronage circuit (Audemars Piguet Contemporary).
network_position.connections: Carsten Nicolai/Alva Noto (shared aesthetic territory), Audemars Piguet Contemporary (major commissioner), Ars Electronica community, 180 Studios London, electronic music and glitch art scenes

potential_role_in_adai.role_detail: Ikeda provides the strongest precedent for making data itself into primary art material at immersive scale. His practice demonstrates that graph/relational data can be experienced sensorially rather than read informationally — essential proof-of-concept for A(DAI)'s vision of a Sense Room where intelligence graph data becomes spatial-sensory experience. His work shows this approach can operate successfully within major institutional contexts.
